//: Codes that count as evidence of a SyntaxError although some valid JavaScript draws them,
because every positive that draws them is a known gap in the pinned tsgo's parser rather
than a sign the code is loose. Read by tooling/census/conformance262.mjs (judgeNegative).
An entry applies only while all of these hold, and the run fails its audit otherwise:
- it has a reason and the tsgo pin it was audited against, and that pin is the one the
compiler under test reports (`nts version`: 'pinned tsgo X'). A gap is true of a
version, not of tsgo: when the pin moves, re-audit every entry -- a fixed gap would
otherwise keep negatives passing for the wrong reason.
- every positive it lists is still in the suite;
- in a whole test/language run, no positive it does NOT list draws the code.
Every run prints how many negatives pass only by an override, beside the pass count: an
override invisible in the summary becomes a threshold.
Agreed with the compiler lane 2026-09-26, on the census of f8628b64.

overrides.reason: tsgo parse gaps on valid JavaScript: Unicode 16/17 identifier characters (its identifier tables predate them), and `in` inside an initializer in a for-of destructuring head. 554 negatives draw TS1005 ('X' expected).
tsgo treats `await` as reserved at the top level of a script, where it is an ordinary identifier (`var await;`). 399 negatives draw TS1109 (Expression expected).
tsgo's identifier tables predate Unicode 16 and 17, so identifier characters those versions added are an Invalid character. 93 negatives draw TS1127.
